videos.title: This AI Tool Adds Music & Sound Effects to Your Video Automatically | Ace Studio
videos.description: Try Ace Studio Here:  acestudio.ai  Ace Studio’s new Video Composer can analyze your video, generate matching music and sound effects, and place everything into a fully editable timeline.   In this video, I walk through exactly how it works, from importing a silent B-roll sequence to generating multiple music options, layering AI-created sound effects, and refining everything directly inside the canvas.  If you’ve ever spent way too long trying to find the right background music, ambient sounds, or scene-specific effects for a video, this feature is aiming to make that process much faster.   Ace Studio analyzes the footage in real time — including cuts, motion, on-screen events, and the environment — then generates music and special effects that fit the scenes.   The generated audio is placed into the timeline as editable clips, so you can still move things around, adjust volume, fade clips in and out, duplicate sections, mute tracks, or delete anything you do not want.  In this demo, I start with a blank project, drag a video into the canvas, and let Ace Studio analyze the clip. From there, I generate a calm music track for the full video, then create a second music track with a more upbeat feel that matches different scenes including the park, the office, and Times Square.   After that, I use Video Composer to generate scene-aware sound effects, then manually refine parts of the timeline by selecting ranges and prompting for more specific ambient audio like pond sounds, park ambiance, and children playing in the background.  One of the biggest takeaways from the video is that Ace Studio is not just generating audio and locking you into the result. The music and sound effects are dropped into the timeline with full editability, which makes the tool feel more like an AI audio assistant for video rather than a one-click black box.  Try Ace Studio here:  acestudio.ai  If you try Video Composer for yourself, let me know what kind of videos you would use it on.  #AceStudio #AIVideo #AIMusic #SoundDesign #VideoEditing #AITools  Chapters  00:00 Intro – Can AI analyze your video and generate matching music + SFX? 00:20 What Ace Studio Video Composer does 00:43 Where to download Ace Studio 2.0 01:03 Starting a blank project and importing footage 01:26 Ace Studio analyzes the video 01:47 Timeline basics and selecting a time range 02:21 Generating a calm music track for the full video 03:00 Listening to the first result 03:17 Adjusting volume and fading clips 03:27 Creating a second, more upbeat music track 04:24 Adding AI-generated sound effects for each scene 05:18 First listen to the sound design pass 05:31 Manually adding more specific scene effects 06:22 Refining transitions and duplicating clips 06:51 Final listen 07:03 Final thoughts on Ace Studio Video Composer 07:28 Why the editable timeline matters 07:45 Outro  Current Kingy review and source notes: https://kingy.ai/news/ace-studio-review-the-all-in-one-ai-music-studio-that-just-learned-to-score-video/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=description&utm_campaign=2nTX3oYyBtM&utm_content=exact_match

videos.title: Karpathy's Wiki vs. Open Brain. One Fails When You Need It Most.
videos.description: Full Comparison w/ Prompts & Open Brain Wiki: https://natesnewsletter.substack.com/p/your-ai-re-derives-everything-it?r=1z4sm5&utm_campaign=post&utm_medium=web&showWelcomeOnShare=true ___________________ What's really happening inside the memory architecture debate when Andre Karpathy's wiki idea got 41,000 bookmarks in a week and everyone is asking if it makes OpenBrain obsolete?  The common story is that these are competing approaches — but the reality is that they solve the same AI amnesia problem from opposite directions, and the difference determines whether your AI gets smarter over time or accumulates more stuff to dig through.  In this video, I share the inside scoop on the deepest design decision in AI knowledge systems:   • Why Karpathy's wiki compiles understanding at write time while OpenBrain synthesizes at query time  • How editorial decisions in wiki synthesis can bake errors into your understanding  • What breaks at scale for each approach and why teams need different architectures  • Where the hybrid solution lives with a graph database over structured data  Builders who pick a memory architecture without understanding this fork will either lose detail when they need precision or burn tokens re-deriving connections they already made.  Chapters 00:00 41,000 bookmarks and hundreds of DMs 02:30 The insight underneath the simplicity 05:00 Why AI throws away its cognitive work every time 07:30 Knowledge compiled once vs re-derived on every query 10:00 Write time vs query time: the fundamental fork 13:00 Study guide vs filing cabinet with librarian 16:00 The editorial trap in wiki synthesis 19:00 Dashboards hide exactly the thing you need to see 22:00 Where Karpathy's wiki wins: deep research mode 25:00 Where OpenBrain wins: precise structured operations 28:00 Multi-agent access and volume scaling 31:00 Where each system breaks at scale 34:00 Wiki stillness vs database stillness 36:30 The hybrid: OpenBrain graph database plugin 39:00 AI as maintainer, not oracle 41:00 Making the decision for your context layer  Subscribe for daily AI strategy and news. videos.title: How I Built an AI Newsletter Agent with CREAO (Step-by-Step)
videos.description: Resources: CREAO:  https://agent.creao.ai/@derekcheungsa Kit API Documentation: https://developers.kit.com/api-reference/broadcasts/create-a-broadcast Sign-up to free newsletter: https://aifornoncoders.com/newsletter  Learn how to build an AI newsletter agent with CREAO that researches trends, pulls YouTube videos, and sends newsletters via Kit — all from one conversation. In this CREAO tutorial, I'll show you how to go from a simple chat prompt to a permanent, scheduled Agent that teaches itself new APIs from documentation.  CREAO is an AI Super Agent that lets you build automated workflows using natural language — no code, no terminal, no API key configuration. In this video, we build a personalized newsletter generator step by step: first as a simple Gmail workflow, then we lock it into a permanent Agent with one click, schedule it to run every morning, add a YouTube channel as a source, and finally teach CREAO the Kit (ConvertKit) API from a documentation URL. The result is a fully automated newsletter system that compounds over time — every API you teach CREAO becomes a permanent Skill available to all future Agents.  What makes CREAO different from ChatGPT, Claude, Manus, or n8n is that what you build outlives the conversation. The workflow doesn't die when you close the chat — it becomes a permanent, scheduled tool that runs without being reinvented each time. This tutorial demonstrates the full Solve - Solidify - Scale workflow, plus the Auto-API Integration feature where CREAO learns any API from its documentation and saves it as a reusable Skill.
